name: upgrade_pydantic_validate_all_to_validate_default
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: validate_all=True to 2.x ConfigDict(validate_default=True) - the v1 key is silently ignored under pydantic 2.x, so a field's own invalid DEFAULT value is never actually run through its validator; incomplete-fix broken correctly migrates the validator decorator to @field_validator but replaces the config with an unrelated, also-plausible-looking extra='forbid' hardening flag instead of validate_default=True
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). Stock in stock.py defaults quantity to an invalid value (-1) and relies on pydantic 1.x `class Config: validate_all = True` to make sure even the DEFAULT value gets run through quantity_must_be_nonneg (normally pydantic skips validating values that were never actually supplied). Under the installed pydantic 2.x, validate_all is silently ignored (unrecognized), so `Stock()` no longer raises - the bad default slips through uncaught. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(validate_default=True)`, and update the validator itself to the `@field_validator` + `@classmethod` pydantic 2.x pattern. `Stock()` (no arguments) must raise a validation error; `Stock(quantity=5)` must still work.

test_setup_files.test_stock.py:
from stock import Stock

try:
    Stock()
    raise AssertionError("expected the invalid default quantity (-1) to be rejected")
except AssertionError:
    raise
except Exception:
    pass

s = Stock(quantity=5)
assert s.quantity == 5

print("PASS")
